title: 0x and 0o integers past 64 bits are exact or refused, never rounded
notes: The Core schema reads a plain scalar that matches `[-+]?[0-9]+` as an integer and gives that pattern no upper bound (section 10.3.2). A library therefore either returns the exact integer or refuses the scalar with a limit error that says it is too large; turning it into a float, a string or a wrapped 64-bit number changes the data without a word. A library that reads it gives exactly the expected result; one that refuses it says so with a limit error. A crash, a hang, a wrong result, or more than the stated time or memory fails. The resource bounds are the robustness requirement of the kit, not a rule of the specification. This case uses the Core `0x` and `0o` forms (`0x[0-9a-fA-F]+`, `0o[0-7]+`), which have no bound either.

provenance.reference: Hexadecimal and octal integers past 64 bits read as strings, floats or wrapped numbers in several libraries.
